title: Allocation of Funds for Primary Education
body_text:
State-wise detail of funds allocated for elementary education under Samagra Shiksha during the last three years and the current year is at Annexure .
Financial assistance is provided to States and UTs for implementation of the interventions under Samagra Shiksha. Accordingly, annual plans under Samagra Shiksha are prepared by the States and UTs based on their requirements and priority and this is reflected in their respective Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWP&B). These plans are then appraised and approved/estimated by Project Approval Board (PAB) in consultation with the States and UTs as per the programmatic and financial norms of the scheme. The funds are released based on the fulfilment of certain conditions such as pace of expenditure, receipt of commensurate State share, audited accounts, statement cumulative State share, statement on outstanding advances, up-to date expenditure statement, furnishing of information as prescribed in the Manual on Financial Management & Procurement and audited utilization certificate of previous year. The unspent balances of last year are taken into account while releasing the funds. Some of the States are not able to receive all instalments owing to the slow pace of their expenditure.
This Department has launched the PRABANDH (Project Appraisal, Budgeting Achievements and Data Handling) System. One of the important features of the PRABANDH System is updation of Expenditure incurred under the different interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. For this purpose, a data visualization Dashboard has been created in the PRABANDH System for display of monthly status of physical and financial progress under the major interventions of the Samagra Shiksha. Regular follow ups and review meetings are held with the States/UTs ensuring an integrated approach for monitoring and smooth implementation of the schemes.

The cess levied for specific purposes under any law made by Parliament is levied and collected by the Government of India and does not form part of the divisible pool of taxes and accordingly not distributed between the Union and the States in terms of Article 270 of the Constitution of India.
For the education sector, the utilization of the proceeds is put through reserve funds viz. Prarambhik Shikha Kosh (PSK) and Madhyamik and Uchchtar Shiksha Kosh (MUSK). Details of Utilization of PSK and MUSK is as under:

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply dated 10 August 2026, the Ministry of Education detailed state-wise fund allocations under Samagra Shiksha for elementary education over the last three years and the current year, along with expenditure on infrastructure, teacher salaries, textbooks and uniforms for 2024-25 and 2025-26. It also disclosed Education Cess collections (Rs 63,252.86 crore in 2024-25 and Rs 65,890.50 crore in 2025-26) and utilization figures for the Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh (PSK) and Madhyamik and Uchchtar Shiksha Kosh (MUSK) reserve funds. The reply explained the fund release mechanism via Annual Work Plans and Budgets appraised by the Project Approval Board, and highlighted the PRABANDH system used for monitoring physical and financial progress.
enrichment.context:
Samagra Shiksha is the Centre's integrated flagship scheme for school education, subsuming earlier programmes like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) and Teacher Education, covering education from pre-school to senior secondary level. It operates on a centrally sponsored scheme model with funds shared between the Centre and States/UTs, released based on conditions like expenditure pace, matching state share, and audited utilization certificates. The Project Approval Board (PAB) mechanism and the PRABANDH (Project Appraisal, Budgeting, Achievements and Data Handling) portal are key governance tools ensuring accountability and real-time monitoring of scheme implementation across states.

The reply also sheds light on the constitutional and fiscal architecture around cesses. Under Article 270, cesses levied by Parliament for specific purposes are excluded from the divisible pool of taxes shared with States, unlike regular taxes recommended for devolution by the Finance Commission. This has been a point of contention in Centre-State fiscal relations, as rising reliance on cesses and surcharges (which are not shared with states) has been flagged by successive Finance Commissions as eroding states' share of the divisible pool. The Education Cess proceeds are routed through dedicated reserve funds—PSK for elementary/primary education and MUSK for secondary/higher education—ensuring earmarked utilization for education sector needs.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding cesses levied by the Government of India:
1. Cesses are part of the divisible pool of taxes shared with States under Article 270 of the Constitution.
2. Proceeds of the Education Cess are routed through dedicated funds such as the Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh and Madhyamik and Uchchtar Shiksha Kosh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, cesses levied for specific purposes do not form part of the divisible pool of taxes under Article 270 and are not shared with states. Education Cess proceeds are utilized through PSK (for elementary education) and MUSK (for secondary/higher education), making statement 2 correct and statement 1 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question:
The 'Samagra Shiksha' scheme of the Ministry of Education integrates which of the following erstwhile schemes?
1. Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
2. Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan
3. Teacher Education
4. Mid-Day Meal Scheme
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
prelims_questions.explanation: Samagra Shiksha integrates Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA), and Teacher Education into a single scheme covering pre-school to senior secondary education. The Mid-Day Meal Scheme (now PM POSHAN) is a separate scheme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the fiscal implications of the growing reliance on cesses and surcharges by the Union Government on the principle of cooperative federalism, with reference to Article 270 of the Constitution.
